topic: Look 4 · Unit 1 + Unit 2 — Function 1: Giving Directions · SB 25 · WB 20 · Grade 4 · 4P2 (periods 5–6, Thu 24/09/2026)
title: Look 4 · Unit 1 + Unit 2 — Function 1 (giving directions)
subtitle: Left, right, straight — say it clearly and they will find you 🧭

features.title: Six Words That Move You
features.desc: Turn, go straight, go past, follow, continue, corner — the words that move a person through a place.

features.title: A Map and a Message
features.desc: Read written directions, follow them in order, and land on the one right place.

features.title: Three Games
features.desc: Scramble the words, match each phrase to its job, sort the moves by what they do.

features.title: Say It, Walk It
features.desc: Give your partner a real route out loud — then follow theirs without looking.

method.phase: Vocab → Route → Game → Review (Function 1 of the unit-1-and-2 session)

games.name: Direction Word Scramble
games.why: production under a clock — the hint is the meaning, so the word is retrieved, not copied

games.name: Phrase & Job Match
games.why: paired recall — the phrase and the job it does are stored as one chunk, which is how a route is remembered

games.name: Go, Turn or Where It Is
games.why: metacognitive sorting — the learner has to name what each phrase does to the walker before using it

voice: Say it LOUD. Say it WRONG. But SAY IT.
A direction you can say is a direction someone else can follow.

storyline: A new student cannot find the music room at the school gate. Linh gives directions too fast and they fail; Nam gives them in the group chat in the wrong order and they fail too. The class fixes both by learning the four sentence shapes — then reads a map, and ends by walking a route out loud.

rooms.title: The Entrance
rooms.label: Warm-Up
rooms.content:
One class, one route 🧭 By the end you can give directions someone else can follow — and read directions someone else wrote.

  • Six moving words: turn, straight, past, follow, continue, corner
  • The four sentence shapes: Go straight. · Turn left. · Follow the path. · Go past the bank.
  • A map you read, and a route you say out loud
  • WB page 20 — you write your own short route
How this lesson works: every room gives you words first and the route second. Say each line out loud as you read it — a direction that stays in your head never gets anyone anywhere.

rooms.title: The Lost Visitor
rooms.label: Scene
rooms.content:
Visitor: Excuse me — where is the music room? 👋
Linh: Go straight along this corridor. Turn left at the stairs. Go past the library. It is on the right.
Visitor: Straight, left, past the library, right. Got it. Thank you!
Linh: Wait — turn left, not right. And that was too fast. Come with me, I will show you.
Nam: That is why I always say the route back first. Say it, then walk it.
🤔 Reality check: Linh's directions were correct and still useless — she said them once, quickly, with no order. A route is a sequence: first go straight, then turn, then go past, then it is on your right.

rooms.title: The Group Chat
rooms.label: Text Scene
rooms.content:
Linh: where are you? the presentation starts in 5 😬
Nam: outside the wrong building. your directions were a map of chaos
Linh: ok. go straight, do not turn. go past the bakery. turn left at the corner 🔁
Nam: past the bakery, then LEFT at the corner. ok walking
Linh: continue straight past the park. the sports centre is on your right. we are next to it ✅
Nam: found you. that took 4 minutes. the first one took 15 😄
The four shapes that carry a route: Go straight. · Turn left / right. · Go past [a place]. · It is on the left / right. Every direction your teacher gives you is one of those four, or two of them joined with then.

rooms.title: The Words
rooms.label: Learn
rooms.content:
1. turn: change the way you are walking — Turn left at the stairs.
2. straight: forward, without turning — Go straight along the corridor.
3. past: in front of a place, and then continuing — Go past the library.
4. follow: go the same way as someone or something — Follow the path to the gate.
5. continue: keep going, do not stop — Continue straight for 100 metres.
6. corner: the place where two streets meet — Turn right at the corner.
7. route: the way from one place to another — This route goes past the park.
8. on the left / on the right: which side of the street the place is on — The bank is on the left.
The rule in one line: a direction is a verb + a way. Go straight · Turn left · Follow the path · Go past the bank. Give one at a time, in order, and the other person will always arrive.

rooms.title: The Map — Find the Way
rooms.label: Reading
rooms.content:
How to use this room: read the route with your finger on the page — one phrase, one step. The order is the answer.

🗺️ A route to the library

Start at the school gate. Go straight along Nguyen Trai Street. Go past the bakery and the bank. Turn left at the corner. Continue straight past the park. The library is on the right, next to the sports centre.

Now the other way: from the library to the music room. Turn right at the corner, go past the sports centre, and continue straight past the park. The music room is on the left, opposite the bakery.

Follow the route: after you turn left at the corner and continue past the park, where is the library?
Follow the route: you have just turned left at the corner. What do you do next?
🤔 Reality check: the map never says turn twice in a row and never says past without naming the place. Directions are a list — if you lose the order, you lose the person.

rooms.title: The Route — Say It In Order
rooms.label: Route
rooms.content:
How to use this room: a direction is a verb plus a way. Choose the verb that moves the person forward, then check the place that follows it.
Complete the direction: _____ straight along the corridor, then turn left at the stairs.
Choose the best direction: you are walking along the street and the bank is in front of you. You do not want to stop there.
Say it back: before you walk anywhere, repeat the route in your own words — Straight, then left at the stairs, then past the library, then on the right. The repeat catches the mistake before the walker does.

rooms.title: Game 1 — Direction Scramble
rooms.label: Game 1
rooms.content: How to win: the hint under each row is the meaning — read it, then click the tiles in order. A wrong word shakes and clears itself, so nothing is lost.

rooms.title: Game 2 — Phrase & Job
rooms.label: Game 2
rooms.content: How to win: click a phrase on the left, then the job it does on the right. Eight pairs. Wrong pairs shake and let go — guess boldly.

rooms.title: Game 3 — Go, Turn or Where It Is
rooms.label: Game 3
rooms.content:
How to win: click a phrase, then the group it belongs to. Ask one question about each phrase — does it move me on, does it change my direction, or does it only tell me where something is?

The three groups: GO = you keep walking the way you are going · TURN = you change direction · WHERE IT IS = it tells you the place, not the move.

rooms.title: The Test
rooms.label: Test
rooms.content:
Scenario: You are at the school gate. _____ straight, then turn left at the stairs.
Scenario: The bank is in front of you on the same street. You want to keep walking.
Scenario: Your friend says: Turn right at the corner, then continue past the park. What do you do SECOND?

rooms.title: The Key
rooms.label: Mastery
rooms.content:
🎓 You now hold the key
  • Six moving words: turn · straight · past · follow · continue · corner.
  • The four shapes: Go straight. · Turn left / right. · Go past [place]. · It is on the left / right.
  • Order is the meaning: say the steps one at a time, in sequence, and the walker arrives.
  • Go past means walk in front of it and continue — you do not stop at the bank.
  • Say it back first: repeat the route in your own words, then walk it.
Level Up: tonight, give someone at home a real route from your front door to the nearest shop — out loud, in order, using three of the six words. Then let them give you one back, and follow it exactly.
Write it down (WB page 20): write four sentences that take a friend from your school gate to your classroom. Use go straight, turn, go past, and on the left or on the right.
